# 2 Samuel Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 174r–175v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_007_page_001.jpg, 2SA_007_page_002.jpg, 2SA_007_page_003.jpg
**DSS:** 4QSamᵃ (4Q51) fragments extant — significant variants for the Davidic covenant

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** When the king was settled in his house and the LORD had given him rest from all his surrounding enemies, **2** the king said to Nathan the prophet, "See — I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells within curtains."

**3** Nathan said to the king, "Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you."

**4** But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan: **5** "Go and tell my servant David: 'Thus says the LORD: Shall you build me a house to dwell in? **6** I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt to this day, but I have been moving about in a tent and a tabernacle. **7** In all the places where I moved with all the sons of Israel, did I speak a word to any of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built me a house of cedar?"'

**8** "Now therefore say to my servant David: 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel. **9** I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones of the earth. **10** I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. Sons of wickedness shall afflict them no longer, as formerly, **11** from the time I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. Moreover, the LORD declares to you that the LORD will build you a house.

**12** "'When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who shall come from your body, and I will establish his kingdom. **13** He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. **14** I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son. When he commits iniquity, I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men. **15** But my covenant-faithfulness shall not depart from him, as I removed it from Saul, whom I put away before you. **16** Your house and your kingdom shall be established forever before you. Your throne shall be established forever.'"

**17** In accordance with all these words and all this vision, Nathan spoke to David.

**18** Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said, "Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far? **19** And yet this was a small thing in your eyes, O Lord GOD. You have spoken also of your servant's house for a great while to come — and this is the charter for mankind, O Lord GOD!

**20** What more can David say to you? You know your servant, O Lord GOD! **21** For the sake of your word, and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness, to make your servant know it.

**22** Therefore you are great, O LORD God! There is none like you, and there is no God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

**23** And who is like your people Israel — the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem as a people for himself, to make a name for himself, and to do great and awesome things for your land, before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, from nations and their gods?

**24** You established your people Israel for yourself as your people forever, and you, O LORD, became their God.

**25** Now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word you have spoken concerning your servant and his house, and do as you have spoken. **26** May your name be magnified forever, saying, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel,' and may the house of your servant David be established before you.

**27** For you, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed to your servant, saying, 'I will build you a house.' Therefore your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to you.

**28** O Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant. **29** Now may it please you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you. For you, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with your blessing shall the house of your servant be blessed forever."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter is among the most theologically significant in the Hebrew Bible. All three translators agree on the central *bayit* (house) wordplay and the structure of the Davidic covenant: (1) God's reversal of David's temple plan (vv.1-7), (2) the covenant oracle (vv.8-16), and (3) David's prayer of response (vv.18-29). The unconditional nature of the covenant — discipline without abandonment — is consistently rendered by all three.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.2 — "tent of curtains" vs. "curtains" vs. "tent curtains"
- **EMET:** "in-[the]-midst of-the-curtain [yeri'ah]"
- **LOGOS:** "within a tent of curtains"
- **PNEUMA:** "inside tent curtains"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "within curtains" — the Hebrew says *betokh ha-yeri'ah* (within the curtain/tent fabric). LOGOS adds "a tent of" for clarity; the text simply says "curtain."

### V.6 — "moving about" vs. "walking about" vs. "on the move"
- **EMET:** "walking-about [mithalekh]"
- **LOGOS:** "moving about"
- **PNEUMA:** "on the move"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "moving about" — LOGOS. The hitpael *mithalekh* conveys continuous movement. PNEUMA's "on the move" is too colloquial.

### V.7 — "tribes" vs. "leaders"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "tribes [shivtey]"
- **PNEUMA:** "leaders"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "tribes" — following the MT. PNEUMA appears to follow "judges" (*shoftey*), which is the reading of 1 Chr 17:6 and the LXX, but the MT has "tribes." Both are noted.

### V.12 — "offspring" vs. "seed"
- **EMET:** "your-seed [zera']"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "your offspring"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "your offspring" — standard formal rendering of *zera'* when referring to a specific descendant.

### V.14 — "when he does wrong" rendering
- **EMET:** "When he-does-wrong [ba-ha'avotō]"
- **LOGOS:** "When he commits iniquity"
- **PNEUMA:** "When he does wrong"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "When he commits iniquity" — LOGOS preserves the gravity of *avon* (iniquity), which is stronger than generic "wrong."

### V.15 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "steadfast love" vs. "faithful love"
- **EMET:** "covenant-faithfulness [chasdi]"
- **LOGOS:** "steadfast love"
- **PNEUMA:** "faithful love"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "covenant-faithfulness" — project convention for *hesed/chesed* in covenantal contexts.

### V.16 — "established forever before you" vs. "endure forever before you"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "established forever before you"
- **PNEUMA:** "endure forever before you"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "established forever before you" — *ne'eman* from the root *amen* specifically means "made firm/established."

### V.19 — *torat ha-adam*
- **EMET:** "the-instruction [torah] of-the-adam [ha-adam]"
- **LOGOS:** "the charter for mankind"
- **PNEUMA:** "Is this your plan for all humanity?"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the charter for mankind" — the phrase is genuinely obscure. LOGOS's rendering is most balanced between scholarly accuracy and readability. PNEUMA's question form adds interpretation.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
